metadata.readme:
# kt-turtlebot3-host

Editable Kinematic Trees `python` project created from a KTM-installed libkt boilerplate package.

KTM copied this project out of the immutable package store so you can edit it normally. Work in this directory, not in the installed boilerplate package.

For a fresh project, `ktm project run` suffices; `project dev` is not a prerequisite. The sequence below shows the optional development watcher and packaging workflow.

## Start here

```bash
ktm project dev
ktm project test
ktm project run
ktm project pack
```

The generated process is a complete HTTP echo. While `ktm project run` is
running, send a request from another terminal:

```bash
curl --fail-with-body \
  --output /dev/null \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/octet-stream' \
  --data-binary 'Hello from KT' \
  http://127.0.0.1:8080/input

curl --fail-with-body http://127.0.0.1:8080/output
```

The second command prints:

```text
Hello from KT
```

`ktm project dev` is the watched development path (`project run --watch`). It uses the verified dependency graph, prepares the managed environment, builds and runs, and watches coherent source changes until Ctrl-C. Use `ktm project build --watch` to rebuild without launching. A failed or partial save does not replace the last-known-good immutable development revision. Use `ktm project build` when a script or CI job needs one finite convergence, and run `ktm project dev --help` for supported watcher controls.

`ktm project run` selects this project directly. It prepares and builds a verified captured revision before execution.
On Linux, KTM can acquire and start the verified local runtime controller without device enrollment. Offline execution requires the controller package inputs already installed. KTM selects the managed Python environment,
binds imports to the selected source or immutable revision (not a different editable checkout),
passes the selected package manifest and private runtime document as literal
arguments, and invokes Python without a shell. An installed package coordinate
uses the same structured recipe and managed environment.

## Advanced diagnostics

```bash
ktm project build
ktm project inspect --view health
ktm project inspect --view environment
ktm project generate
```

These diagnostic commands are useful when investigating a failure, but they
are not prerequisites for the beginner workflow.

Recommended first edit:

```text
src/kt_turtlebot3_host/process.py
```

The starter is intentionally runnable before you edit it. Its `step` callback
reads every opaque request body from the `input` channel and writes the same
bytes to `output`. Replace that relay with your application behavior. When your
process understands a KT datatype, prefer the generated typed accessors under
`_generated` over raw channel access.

`runtime.json` binds the HTTP transport to localhost port 8080, maps
`POST /input` to the input channel, and maps `GET /output` to the output
channel. The localhost binding keeps this beginner example off external
interfaces unless you deliberately change it.

## Package and runtime roles

The root `package.ktm.json` is the distributable package contract: identity,
dependencies, build recipes, Python compatibility, channels, and configuration
schema. The sibling `runtime.json` is a deployment-instance contract: it links
to `./package.ktm.json` and may supply routing, scheduling, channel policy, and
concrete configuration values. There is no second package definition and no
generated `runtime/` directory.

Starter conformance tests live in the SDK repository instead of every generated
project. `scripts/test.py` still gives developers a fast source/import smoke
check; add application tests as you replace the echo behavior.

For direct SDK debugging:

```bash
python -m kt_turtlebot3_host \
  --package package.ktm.json \
  --runtime runtime.json
```

## Dependency model

The generated `package.ktm.json` directly declares only
`kinematic-trees/kt-python-sdk`, which includes its adapter. The SDK declares the
managed Python tool, libkt and Messages; KTM resolves them recursively for the
selected target and records the exact installed graph. Do not repeat the SDK's
dependencies in this starter. Add direct package dependencies when your own
application needs additional packages.
`pyproject.toml` is your authority for ordinary third-party Python packages.
Add them explicitly under `[project].dependencies`, for example:

```toml
dependencies = ["opencv-python-headless==4.10.0.84"]
```

On `ktm project dev` and `ktm project test`, KTM first installs its integrity-verified graph
wheels, then installs this project and resolves these declared dependencies in
the same managed environment. Project dependencies cannot replace a KTM-owned
distribution. KTM never runs `pip freeze` or writes dependency changes back to
`pyproject.toml`; choose and review version constraints yourself. A clean
machine therefore needs access to the configured Python package index unless
the declaration uses an accessible direct URL.

The starter imports every collision-free datatype namespace:

```python
from kt.messages import *
```

Use the schema namespace to select a generated type, for example
`vision_sample.ImageSample`, so common names such as `Vector3` cannot collide.

You normally do **not** need to export `CPATH`, `LIBRARY_PATH`, `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, `PKG_CONFIG_PATH`, or `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` yourself. KTM supplies those when you use `ktm project dev`, `ktm project build`, and `ktm project test`.

Python calls and source remain portable. The default `source` archive does not vendor managed
Python, `libkt`, the Python SDK, `kt-messages`, or a virtual environment; KTM
installs the declared dependency closure for the selected host environment.
`ktm project pack` preserves `pyproject.toml` byte-for-byte, excludes the managed
environment, and does not freeze or vendor resolved Python dependencies. Pack
can still prepare dependencies while running its build/test qualification. Bare `ktm project pack`
uses this portable source mode. `ktm-pack.json` also retains a
`compiled-source` policy definition; selecting alternative pack modes is not exposed by this v2 CLI. Do not copy dependency artifacts into the process package.

## Environment inspection

```bash
ktm project inspect --view environment
ktm project inspect --view health
```

These are read-only observations of declarations and verified installed inputs.
They do not prepare an environment or emit shell commands. Run authored build,
test and runtime recipes through KTM; there is no v2 `env --shell`/`eval` setup step.
Static inspection is not proof that an application will run. `project run` needs
a compatible local controller; its HTTP echo is the actual runtime check.
